name: Ironforge
summary: Ironforge is carved into the heart of a mountain, in the snows of Dun Morogh. It is the ancient capital of the Bronzebeard dwarves, and one of the Alliance's strongest bulwarks. At its center burns the Great Forge. Here King Magni Bronzebeard rules, and now his halls also shelter the gnomes who lost Gnomeregan.

sections.title: A City of Stone and Fire
sections.body:
Twenty-five centuries ago, the first dwarves awoke in Uldaman. Westward they journeyed, into the jagged peaks of Dun Morogh, and delved into the tallest mountain. There they raised a shrine to their maker, the titan Khaz'goroth, and beside it the Great Forge. And ever since, the city has grown outward in rings around that fiery hearth.

No city above the ground is like it. Ironforge lies wholly beneath stone, warmed by roaring hearths and by rivers of molten rock. Its fortified gates and deep halls have held through centuries of war.

sections.title: The War of the Three Hammers
sections.body:
For generations, three dwarven clans shared the mountain. The Bronzebeards lived beside the Wildhammers and the Dark Irons. When High King Modimus Anvilmar died, a bitter civil war broke out for rule of Ironforge. The Bronzebeards won it, and drove their rivals out.

Then Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan led the Dark Irons back for vengeance. His siege reached the very heart of Ironforge, before the Bronzebeards threw it back. In the south, by mischance, Thaurissan then summoned Ragnaros the Firelord. The Firelord's coming shattered the Redridge Mountains, and doomed Thaurissan's own host. Ever since, the Bronzebeards have held Ironforge unchallenged.

sections.title: Honor to the Alliance
sections.body: In the Second War, the Bleeding Hollow clan overran much of Khaz Modan. But Ironforge held firm behind its sealed gates, until the Alliance of Lordaeron broke the siege. For that debt of honor, King Magni Bronzebeard pledged Ironforge to the Alliance forever. He stood by it even when Gilneas and Quel'Thalas walked away.

sections.title: A Haven for Exiles
sections.body: In the Third War, Magni mourned his brother Muradin, lost in Northrend. When Gnomeregan fell, the king opened his gates to thousands of gnome refugees. Under High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, they carved out Tinker Town within the stone city. And the Deeprun Tram now runs beneath the earth, straight to Stormwind. So Ironforge has become a crossroads of dwarven steel and gnomish invention.

faq.answer: King Magni Bronzebeard rules Ironforge and the kingdom of Khaz Modan from the High Seat. A skilled warrior and master blacksmith, he has governed his people through the Second and Third Wars and remains a deeply loyal pillar of the Alliance. Ironforge remains one of the Alliance's fiercest bulwarks.

faq.q: Why are there so many gnomes in Ironforge?
faq.answer: When the nearby gnomish capital of Gnomeregan fell to a sudden trogg invasion and a disastrous radiation accident, the surviving gnomes fled into Dun Morogh. King Magni welcomed them into Ironforge, granting them an entire quarter of the city now known as Tinker Town.
The Great Forge is the fiery industrial heart of the city, fed by underground waterfalls of molten magma. It surrounds the Great Anvil, where dwarven weaponsmiths craft legendary arms and armor.

faq.q: How do you travel between Ironforge and Stormwind?
faq.answer: Ironforge is connected directly to Stormwind City by the Deeprun Tram, an extraordinary subterranean railway built by gnomish engineering that cuts straight through the mountain bedrock of the Eastern Kingdoms.

faq.q: Has Ironforge ever fallen to an enemy army?
faq.answer: Ironforge has never fallen to an outside invader. Kilrogg Deadeye's Bleeding Hollow clan laid siege to it for months during the Second War, and the Dark Irons fought into the city during the War of the Three Hammers, but the gates and defenders held.

faq.q: Where did the other dwarf clans go?
faq.answer: After the War of the Three Hammers, the defeated Wildhammer clan relocated north into the Wetlands and the Hinterlands, while the hostile Dark Iron clan settled within the Redridge and Blackrock regions under the thrall of the Firelord.

angles.text: Ironforge is the ancestral home of your kin. Its halls honor your people's resilience, their mastery of stone and the sacred lineage that traces back to the titans.
Since the disaster that consumed Gnomeregan, Tinker Town has served as your temporary home and command center as High Tinker Mekkatorque plots the liberation of your city.
The Great Forge is revered across Azeroth as the premier center of metalworking, housing the Great Anvil where master smiths and King Magni himself shape metal into legend.
Linked to Stormwind by the Deeprun Tram, Ironforge is the Alliance's northern anchor and one of its most reliable military fortresses.
